showcase.prompt: Family F: Use all 105 one-input programs: the five leaves x0, 0, 1, 2, 3, and op(left, right) for each op in add, sub, mul, div and each ordered pair of those five leaves. const_fold recursively folds add/sub/mul only when both children are integer literals; it leaves division untouched, including division by zero. Find ALL programs in F whose const_fold equals Code<op (x0) = 1>. Return the sorted list of programs in compact Code<...> notation.
showcase.why_hard: Several syntax-distinct arithmetic programs fold to the same canonical code value, while division does not fold.

showcase.check: Compare decoded original and transformed outcomes for all 72 programs and inputs 0..6.
showcase.prompt: Family F: Use all 72 one-input programs sub(e, e) and mul(e, 0), where e is any of the four leaves x0, 0, 1, 2 or op(left, right) for op in add, div and each ordered pair of those four leaves. simplify_unsafe recursively folds literal-literal add/sub/mul and rewrites sub(e, e), mul(e, 0), and mul(0, e) to literal 0 before evaluation, even when evaluating e would fail. Evaluation is strict: binary operations evaluate the left child then the right child; div(x, 0) returns Bottom(div_zero). Each executed arithmetic atom costs one layer-0 step. Does simplify_unsafe preserve meaning on F for every x0 in 0..6? If not, give the number of failing programs, the smallest counterexample by expression node count then printed text, its first failing input, and the two outcomes.
showcase.why_hard: Strict evaluation can fail before a cancellation or zero multiplication; every generated source must be checked.

showcase.check: Decode all 224 originals and folds; compare all 1568 outcomes and sum their exact kernel steps.
showcase.prompt: Family F: Start with the five leaves x0, 0, 1, 2, 3; then all 100 binary trees op(left, right) in op order add, sub, mul, div and leaf order as listed; then the first 94 add(left, right) with left from the first 25 binary trees and right from the five leaves in nested order; then sub(div(x0, 0), div(x0, 0)); then 12 let saved = add(2, 3) in add(tree, saved) for binary trees 0..11; then 12 case { is_zero(x0) -> add(2, 3); else -> tree } for those same trees. const_fold recursively folds add/sub/mul only when both children are integer literals; it leaves division untouched, including division by zero. Strict evaluation executes only the selected case arm, binds let once, evaluates binary children left to right, and div(x, 0) returns Bottom(div_zero). Each executed layer-0 arithmetic atom and is_zero test costs one step; skipped branches and literal/variable evaluation cost zero. For every program in F and each x0 in 0..6, give total layer-0 steps before and after const_fold, the exact saving, and whether every outcome is equal.
showcase.why_hard: The domain has 1568 runs, including Bottom(div_zero), bound values and evaluated branches.
